extracted.intended_audience: general readers, journalists, researchers, and policymakers interested in TikTok, platform safety, and tech policy
extracted.subtask_description: A comprehensive overview and assessment of controversies, regulatory findings, and alleged harms associated with TikTok, covering privacy, data access, content moderation, child safety, mental-health impacts, national security, and corporate practices. Useful for evaluating the platform's risk profile and regulatory compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: National security / influence operations risk
rubrics_metrics.description: “The possibility that the Chinese government could use [TikTok] to control data collection on millions of users or control the recommendation algorithm, which could be used for influence operations,”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Concerns about foreign state control or influence via data access or algorithmic manipulation; cited by intelligence/community leaders and lawmakers as a basis for bans and legislative action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Access to user data of protesters and activists
rubrics_metrics.description: Filing said the committee accessed the user data of protesters, civil rights activists and their supporters, including users who had been identified from prior protests; monitored Hong Kong users who uploaded protest-related content.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allegations that company/third parties used internal logs to identify and monitor politically sensitive users; relevant to human-rights and surveillance evaluations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data storage location and cross-border transfers
rubrics_metrics.description: “TikTok Confirms Some U.S. User Data Is Stored In China” / reports of data transfers to China and EU investigations into transfers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where user data is stored/transferred is used to assess legal jurisdiction, compliance with local laws (e.g., GDPR), and exposure to foreign government requests or demands.

rubrics_metrics.name: Efficacy of claimed data-protection measures (Project Texas/Project Clover)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reports and coverage of Project Texas and Project Clover as TikTok's plans to remain operational in the United States and to allay China security fears.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluates whether operational or contractual fixes meaningfully prevent foreign access to data or algorithm control; includes scrutiny of technical, legal, and governance safeguards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alleged use of TikTok for election influence
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims and reporting that China used TikTok to influence U.S. elections and concerns raised by lawmakers and agencies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assesses potential for political manipulation via algorithmic amplification, targeted content, or misinformation campaigns; often cited in policy debates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collection of device identifiers and policy violations
rubrics_metrics.description: “TikTok Tracked User Data Using Tactic Banned by Google” and “collected device identifiers for over a year in violation of Android policies.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Technical-privacy evaluation focusing on telemetry, persistent identifiers, and adherence to platform store policies (e.g., Android/iOS) and their implications for tracking.

rubrics_metrics.name: In-app browser security (keystroke monitoring)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reports that TikTok's in-app browser can monitor your keystrokes, including passwords and credit cards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Security assessment of embedded webviews or in-app browsers and their ability to exfiltrate sensitive information; implications for user credential safety and financial data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Children's data protection / COPPA compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Allegations, lawsuits and settlements relating to abusing children's privacy, including FTC/COPPA claims and a $1.1M settlement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Legal and policy criterion: whether the platform complies with child-data protections, obtains parental consent where required, and follows settlement/FTC orders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulatory enforcement and fines (EU/UK/others)
rubrics_metrics.description: Multiple probes and fines: EU fines (hundreds of millions of euros), ICO fines in the UK (£12.7m), and other national investigations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tracks outcomes of official investigations and fines as indicators of noncompliance with data-protection, advertising, or consumer-protection law.

rubrics_metrics.name: Surveillance of journalists
rubrics_metrics.description: Reports that journalists' data was accessed by employees of its parent company and investigations by the FBI and DOJ into alleged surveillance of journalists.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assesses whether internal access policies were violated and whether the platform enabled improper monitoring of press sources or investigative subjects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Algorithmic recommendation causing harm (suicide, eating disorders)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reports and research showing TikTok's algorithm keeps pushing suicide to vulnerable kids and promotes posts about eating disorders and suicide.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluation of recommendation systems for amplifying self-harm or disordered-eating content; includes analysis of cascade effects and platform response policies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mental-health impacts on teens (tics, anxiety, body image)
rubrics_metrics.description: Coverage linking TikTok content to development of tics, negative body image, and other teen mental-health problems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assesses correlations between platform content consumption and observed mental-health harms in youth; includes clinical reports and epidemiological studies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Promotion of dangerous viral trends affecting public health / supply chains
rubrics_metrics.description: Viral trends on TikTok led to Ozempic shortages as influencers promoted weight-loss uses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluates platform's capacity to drive real-world behavior with public-health implications, including medication shortages and unsafe medical trends.

rubrics_metrics.name: Facilitation of child sexual exploitation and sexual livestreams
rubrics_metrics.description: BBC reporting that TikTok profited from sexual livestreams involving children and subsequent national probes and takedown orders.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assesses moderation effectiveness, detection and removal of child sexual exploitation content, and platform monetization structures that may enable abuse.

rubrics_metrics.name: Harassment, bullying, and creator safety
rubrics_metrics.description: Creators say they are being bullied and the company isn't helping; reports of creators fearing bans and harassment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measures how well the platform prevents, detects, and responds to harassment and protects creators from abusive campaigns and doxxing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discriminatory suppression of marginalized creators
rubrics_metrics.description: Reports that TikTok admitted to suppressing videos from some persons with disabilities and the LGBTQ2 community.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluates content-moderation policies and algorithmic impacts that result in disproportionate suppression of protected groups; includes audits and whistleblower accounts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Censorship and political content moderation bias
rubrics_metrics.description: Allegations and reporting about TikTok blocking pro-Palestinian content, Epstein and anti-Trump videos, and other politically sensitive removals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assesses transparency, consistency, and political neutrality in moderation decisions; relevant to free-speech and geopolitical concerns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Algorithmic transparency and regulatory inquiries
rubrics_metrics.description: EU and other bodies requesting information from TikTok and other platforms on content algorithms; formal investigations into content-breach risks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Criterion: willingness and ability to disclose algorithmic operation, data flows, and moderation decision-making to regulators and independent auditors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acceptability for official devices and government use
rubrics_metrics.description: Top EU bodies and various governments banning TikTok on staff phones or restricting official devices over security reasons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assesses whether the platform meets governmental security standards for official use and whether it should be restricted on government-managed devices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corporate governance, workplace culture and internal practices
rubrics_metrics.description: Reports of toxic work culture, allegations of racism and intense productivity leading to employee harm.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluates company practices, internal culture, employee treatment, and transparency — relevant to corporate responsibility and reputational risk.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legal/legislative measures and policy responses (bans, sell-or-be-banned)
rubrics_metrics.description: Legislative actions, executive orders, and 'sell-or-be-banned' measures debated or passed in various jurisdictions, including U.S. Congress votes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Outcome-oriented measure: extent to which policymakers enact restrictions, which in turn reflects perceived platform risk and shapes compliance obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Platform partnerships and commercial influence
rubrics_metrics.description: TikTok partnerships with tourism bodies, sports teams, and events (e.g., FIFA, United Airlines, Wrexham A.F.C.), used to promote content and services.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assesses commercial reach and reputational integration with public institutions; relevant to brand safety and influence through sponsored content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ability to disrupt communities and creators through service changes
rubrics_metrics.description: Creators say bans and policy shifts would almost certainly disrupt the organic communities they've built.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measures the platform's centrality to creator livelihoods and community formation, and the potential harm when services are restricted or changed abruptly.
